story_clusters.headline: Carney and Alberta's Smith sign landmark pipeline and carbon pricing deal targeting 2027 construction start
story_clusters.summary: Prime Minister Carney and Alberta Premier Danielle Smith signed an implementation agreement in Calgary on May 15 setting a fall 2027 target for construction approval of a new West Coast bitumen pipeline carrying over one million barrels per day, paired with a revised industrial carbon pricing framework capping Alberta's price at $130 per tonne by 2040 — well below the previously planned $170. The deal drew immediate criticism from environmental groups, B.C., the Bloc Québécois, and the NDP as a 'climate capitulation,' while Poilievre called it insufficient because any carbon price remains. B.C.'s energy minister objected to being excluded from negotiations.

story_clusters.headline: Carney unveils national electricity strategy to double grid capacity by 2050, with expanded role for natural gas
story_clusters.summary: Prime Minister Carney announced Canada's long-awaited National Electricity Strategy on May 14, aiming to double the country's grid capacity by 2050 and lower household energy costs. The plan grants more flexibility to natural gas plants and adjusts clean electricity regulations, drawing criticism that it retreats from the 2030 climate targets. Carney said federal facilitation could also help Quebec and Newfoundland resolve the Churchill Falls hydro dispute.

story_clusters.headline: Alberta separatist petition quashed by court; Carney visits province amid secession controversy
story_clusters.summary: An Alberta court ruled that separatists had not followed proper procedure in collecting referendum signatures, quashing their petition in a blow to the independence movement. Prime Minister Carney flew to Calgary days later, saying the best place for Alberta is in Canada while also asserting that any independence referendum must comply with the federal Clarity Act and respect Indigenous rights. Premier Smith called the ruling 'anti-democratic.'

story_clusters.headline: Polling shows deepening Liberal lead as Poilievre's image continues to slide
story_clusters.summary: Multiple polls released this week show the Liberals holding a 11-15 point lead over the Conservatives. Pierre Poilievre's net favourability sits at -13% versus Carney's +20%, and analysis shows Poilievre features in only 9.5% of Conservative MPs' social media posts, suggesting caucus distancing. Commentators debate whether Poilievre can recover, with some comparing his position to Harper's difficult 2004 rebuilding period.

story_clusters.headline: New York Times caught using AI-generated fake quote attributed to Poilievre, tightens freelancer AI policy
story_clusters.summary: An April 15 New York Times article about Carney's majority government contained an AI-hallucinated quote attributed to Conservative leader Pierre Poilievre — a fabrication that ran for over two weeks before correction on May 1. The incident, in which the Times' own Canada bureau chief used AI to generate a summary of Poilievre's views presented as a direct quote, prompted the paper to issue a formal warning to freelancers about AI use.

story_clusters.headline: Bank of Canada sees modest AI productivity gains, holds rates amid Iran war and tariff uncertainty
story_clusters.summary: Bank of Canada Deputy Governor Michelle Alexopoulos delivered a widely covered speech on AI's economic impact, finding early signs of modest productivity gains but no evidence yet of widespread job displacement. Separately, minutes from the April 29 rate decision showed the Governing Council felt it could afford to be patient and hold rates steady at 2.25%, while weighing inflation risks from soaring oil prices due to the Iran war against potential economic weakness from U.S. tariffs.

story_clusters.headline: Ontario Liberal nomination dispute over Erskine-Smith's Scarborough Southwest loss triggers party controversy
story_clusters.summary: Federal Liberal MP Nate Erskine-Smith narrowly lost the Ontario Liberal nomination for the Scarborough Southwest provincial byelection to businessman Ahsanul Hafiz, then filed an appeal alleging irregular voting including possible mass membership sign-ups and extra ballots. The Ontario Liberal Party stood by the result. Erskine-Smith subsequently announced he would resign his federal seat this summer and abandon further candidacy, while the controversy was described as an 'unhelpful distraction' for a party trying to rebuild.

story_clusters.headline: Canada deepens Arctic and Nordic defense ties as Carney pivots toward Europe and middle powers
story_clusters.summary: Canada is actively deepening security cooperation with Nordic countries as part of Prime Minister Carney's broader strategy to build alliances among 'middle powers' in an era of reduced U.S. reliability. Separately, analysis notes Carney's government has made at least nine ministerial visits to Persian Gulf nations, seeking diplomatic, security, and AI cooperation beyond investment. Coverage frames these moves as part of a deliberate post-U.S. realignment.

story_clusters.headline: CSIS visits Quebec firearms manufacturer after Canadian sniper rifles surface in Russia
story_clusters.summary: The Canadian Security Intelligence Service met with Cadex Defence, a Quebec-based firearms manufacturer, after its sniper rifles appeared in Russia in apparent violation of export sanctions. Company president Serge Dextraze told Global News the firearms were fraudulently diverted, as Canada banned weapons exports to Russia following the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. CSIS confirmed it has been working with manufacturers to prevent Russia from illicitly acquiring Canadian-origin goods.

story_clusters.headline: New federal NDP leader Avi Lewis tours Saskatchewan, tensions emerge with provincial NDP over energy policy
story_clusters.summary: Newly elected federal NDP leader Avi Lewis conducted a five-day, eleven-stop Saskatchewan tour, visiting Indigenous communities including Cowessess First Nation to hear about unresolved land claims. Provincial NDP leader Carla Beck declined to meet with Lewis, reflecting tensions over his fossil fuel transition stance versus Saskatchewan's energy realities. Lewis also pushed back on the Carney government's new AI data centres and demanded release of a secret policing deal with China.

story_clusters.headline: Toronto and Montreal compete to host new NATO-aligned Defence, Security and Resilience Bank
story_clusters.summary: Canada was selected to host headquarters for the Defence, Security and Resilience Bank, which will provide long-term financing for defence projects and is expected to bring 3,500 jobs and open by end of 2026. Ontario Premier Doug Ford rallied business leaders for Toronto's bid, while Quebec politicians accused Toronto of waging a 'fear campaign' by invoking the spectre of Quebec separation. Ford disputed this characterization while backing Toronto. Minister Joly, as an MP from Montreal, acknowledged personal bias toward her home city.

story_clusters.headline: Quebec UPAC anti-corruption unit meets PLQ leader Charles Milliard amid leadership race probe
story_clusters.summary: Quebec's anti-corruption unit UPAC met with provincial Liberal leader Charles Milliard in connection with its investigation into the Quebec Liberal Party's leadership race that brought Pablo Rodriguez to the helm last year. Separately, MNA Sona Lakhoyan Olivier apologized in tears to the National Assembly after the ethics commissioner found she had used her constituency office for partisan purposes during that same leadership contest.

story_clusters.headline: Carney, Minister Joly receive Artemis II moon mission crew at Canadian Space Agency
story_clusters.summary: Prime Minister Carney and Industry Minister Mélanie Joly met with the crew of the Artemis II mission — which had recently returned from the far side of the moon — at the Canadian Space Agency's Longueuil headquarters. The visit was framed as a celebration of Canada's participation in the historic mission, featuring astronaut Jeremy Hansen.

story_clusters.headline: Honda cancels $15-billion EV project in Ontario; Carney calls decision 'disappointing'
story_clusters.summary: Honda Canada announced it would not proceed with a planned $15-billion electric vehicle manufacturing project in Alliston, Ontario — its first-ever annual corporate loss year at $2.7 billion. Prime Minister Carney called the decision 'disappointing' while asserting the global EV transition will continue. Honda Canada noted it had not received any of the committed federal funding.

story_clusters.headline: Carney government signals openness to privatizing federal airports and ports
story_clusters.summary: A government discussion paper and Carney's public comments this week indicated openness to selling or amalgamating federal ports, with airports also cited as potential privatization candidates to recycle capital into new infrastructure. Pension funds have long eyed federal infrastructure as ideal long-term assets. Carney said port reform was not a 'top priority' but confirmed the government is open to selling public assets.

story_clusters.headline: Nova Scotia Liberal Party gains with ex-PC justice minister Becky Druhan joining ahead of leadership race
story_clusters.summary: Becky Druhan, a former Progressive Conservative justice minister and Independent MLA for Lunenburg West, joined the Nova Scotia Liberal Party and announced her intention to run for party leadership, adding momentum to the Liberals' provincial rebuild.

story_clusters.headline: BC Conservative leadership race enters final weeks with voter verification controversy
story_clusters.summary: The British Columbia Conservative Party leadership race is in its final weeks before voting closes May 23-29, with five candidates including Peter Milobar competing. A controversy emerged over the party's use of a U.S.-based company to verify voter identities, prompting some members to refuse to participate. The party defended the measure as essential for election security.

story_clusters.headline: Quebec pre-election dynamics: PLQ-PQ polls close, CAQ gains, PQ leader alleges federal spying
story_clusters.summary: With Quebec's October election approaching, multiple polls show a tight three-way race between the PLQ, PQ, and a rebounding CAQ. PQ leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon alleged this week that Ottawa may be spying on his party, drawing widespread skepticism. The Bloc Québécois condemned federal energy policy concessions and called for greater Quebec cultural media support, while Carney's Liberals showed dominant federal polling numbers in Quebec at ~49%.
